newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo Bourse index up, but Nera, Fokus down.
newsitem.headline: Oslo Bourse index up, but Nera, Fokus down.

text.p: The Norwegian all-share index edged higher in brisk turnover on Friday but telecommunications group Nera and Fokus Bank both lost ground.
Oslo's Total index closed 0.3 percent higher at 1,075.09 points in turnover worth 1.40 billion crowns.
Nera continued to slip on a profit warning issued on Thursday following exaggerated profit forecasts, closing 4.8 percent lower at 307.50 crowns. It was the second most traded share at 152 million.
One broker said U.S. investors were selling Nera and he did not recommend buying the share at current levels.
"I think it will fall maybe another 10 percent," he said.
Fokus Bank closed 4.8 percent off at 69 crowns in a sign the market was becoming sceptical the hostile takeover attempt by Sparebankgruppen savings banks would succeed.
The group has offered to buy Fokus at 73 crowns per share.
"Unless there is a counter-bid from someone else the share will fall further," one broker said.
Industrial group Dyno Industrier was up 1.71 percent at 178 crowns after presenting good first-quarter results and a plan to increase profits by the year 2000.
